title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§6 of the 'Teichmülleries' notes). X_n is a sphere carrying the regular n-gon map. The polygon is the equator, with vertices R_i and edge-midpoints Q_{a_i}; P_+ and P_- are the two face centres. X_n^* is X_n with the vertices removed, and D_n is the symmetry group of the map. The quotient map g_n : X_n → X_0 = P^1_C sends vertices to 0, edge-midpoints to 1 and face centres to ∞.

The page finishes computing the induced isomorphism from the 'fundamental group of X_n^* relative to D_n, based at P_{n+}' (the orbifold fundamental group of X_n^*/D_n) to the orbifold fundamental group of P^1 with ramification ∞ at 0, 2 at 1 and n at ∞. That group is Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n>, where Π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) = <ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ | product = 1>.

From the previous page: (*) g_n(ρ) = ρ_∞^{-1}, where ρ is the rotation generator, and (**) g_n(σ_{a_0}) = ρ_1, where σ_{a_0} is the half-turn about the edge-midpoint Q_{a_0}. Since ε_0 = σ_{a_0}ρ, one gets g_n(ε_0) = ρ_1^{-1}ρ_∞^{-1} = (ρ_∞ρ_1)^{-1} = ρ_0. This is the summary (98).

The target group is the free product Z/2 * Z/n, i.e. the (2,n,∞) triangle group or Hecke group; for n = 3 it is PSL_2(Z). In Grothendieck's terms it is the oriented cartographic group with the extra relation ρ_∞^n, i.e. maps all of whose faces are n-gons; the next page calls it the 'polygonal' cartographic group.

(99) extends this to the version with orientation-reversing symmetries, adjoining τ (complex conjugation). The source is Π_n^{D,τ} = Π_n^D ⋊ {1, σ̃_{a_0}}, where σ̃_{a_0} is the reflection of X_n in the great circle P_∞ Q_{a_0} P_∞'. The target is (Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n>) ⋊ {1, τ}, i.e. the extended triangle/Hecke group.

The margin NB records how the reflection τ_∞ acts: ρ_0 ↦ ρ_0^{-1}, ρ_1 ↦ ρ_1^{-1}, and ρ_∞ ↦ (a conjugate by ρ_0 of) ρ_∞^{-1}. He cross-references formula (80) for n = 3 and notes that τ_∞ = τ_{a_0} by definition.

To determine g_n on σ̃_{a_0} he uses the path P' = σ̃°(P) → P given by αα'^{-1}. He deforms it to a path crossing the barycentric 1-skeleton exactly once, on P_+Q_{a_0}, which maps to the real arc (∞,1). The next page concludes g_n(σ̃_{a_0}) = τ_0 and g_n(τ_{a_0}) = τ_∞ (formula (100)).

Purpose: identify the 'polygonal' cartographic group π^τ_n with the orbifold π_1 of the quotient of the regular-polygon map. This prepares §7, which reinterprets these groups in terms of maps (cartes).
errors: The previous page writes the quotient as Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^2>; it should be ρ_∞^n. It also says ρ_1 and ρ_1^{-1} are 'conjugate', whereas they are actually equal since ρ_1^2 = 1.

Conventions on the product relation are implicit. The equality (ρ_∞ρ_1)^{-1} = ρ_0 requires ρ_0ρ_∞ρ_1 = 1, a cyclic form of ρ_∞ρ_1ρ_0 = 1. This must be read consistently with the NB formula τ_∞(ρ_∞) = ρ_0ρ_∞^{-1}ρ_0^{-1}, which holds under that convention.
The NB formula for τ_∞(ρ_∞) is written abbreviated as 'ρ_0(ρ_∞^{-1})'. It must mean conjugation by ρ_0 of ρ_∞^{-1}, not a product; otherwise it is wrong.
The ramification divisor is written '∞{0}' for infinite ramification at 0. That is fine as orbifold notation, but it means 0 is a puncture, not a branch point.

ideas.what: Identification of the orbifold fundamental group of (sphere minus vertices)/symmetry group of the regular n-gon map with Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n> ≅ Z/2 * Z/n, with explicit images of the rotation and half-turn generators
ideas.modern_name: (2,n,∞) triangle group / Hecke group; orbifold fundamental group of a quotient orbifold
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hecke (1936) for Hecke groups; Jones–Singerman (1978) for maps and triangle groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartographic groups and m-gonal maps only in general terms

ideas.what: Extension with reflections: relative fundamental groupoid with τ ≅ semidirect product with {1, τ}, reflection mapped to τ_0, and explicit action of τ_∞ on ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞
ideas.modern_name: extended triangle group / extended Hecke group; non-oriented cartographic group

ideas.what: Computing images of path classes by counting crossings of the barycentric subdivision's 1-skeleton (crossing arc (∞,1) gives ρ_1, etc.)
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial computation of monodromy via the barycentric triangulation (flag/dart model)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a careful but routine computation identifying the symmetry orbifold group of the regular n-gon map with the (extended) Hecke/triangle group (2,n,∞). This is standard and well documented in the maps/dessins literature; it is of mild interest only as a detail of Grothendieck's unpublished §6 setup.
transcription_corrections: 'X_n^{αα}' should almost certainly read X_n^{**} (the subspace minus the barycentric 1-skeleton, as on the previous page).
'(1 →^{g_n} (α,1))' should read '(→^{g_n} (∞,1))', i.e. the arc P_+Q_{a_0} maps to the real arc (∞,1).
'X_0' is underbraced with 'P^1_C' (written Π_{1C} in the hand).
In the NB, τ_∞(ρ_∞) = ρ_0(ρ_∞^{-1}) should read ρ_0ρ_∞^{-1}ρ_0^{-1}, i.e. conjugation by ρ_0; the margin also says 'ici τ_∞ = τ_{a_0} par définition'.
The right-hand side of (99) ends with {1, τ̃_{a_0}}, or {1, τ}, as the adjoined reflection.
'son image dans π_1(X_n^*, D_n×{1,τ}; P) est définie par le chemin' — the base point is written P.
